title: Console core launch: trim advanced observability features to deliver a stable parse-able MVP
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket documents the decision and acceptance criteria for reducing the initial Console observability surface for launch. We will restrict dashboards, tracing, and cost breakdowns to essential, supported views that can be implemented without additional telemetry pipeline changes or long-term storage commitments.
background: During scoping we identified multiple advanced features (custom dashboards, long-term retention, per-token cost breakdown, synthetic transaction alerts) that would add several unblockable dependencies: telemetry pipeline upgrades, additional infra for retention, and a security review for sharing token-level data. To meet launch timing and reduce operational risk, we propose conservative cuts and clear acceptance criteria for the minimal feature set.
decisions: Ship a constrained dashboards surface focused on model-level and route-level summaries only (no custom widgets or drag/drop editing)
Provide a lightweight tracing UI that shows request-level timelines and queue/batch intervals; defer span-level flamegraphs and deep stack traces
Expose a cost breakdown page limited to aggregated per-model and per-route totals for selectable time ranges; defer token-level and user-level cost drilldowns
Defer advanced features (custom dashboards, alerting, retention >30d, synthetic checks, federated dashboards) to post-launch projects and add to backlog with cross-team dependencies
Require engineering sign-off that all shipped views only use existing telemetry indices and do not require new pipeline transformations
scope_included: Dashboard: model summary card (requests, P50, P95 latency, error rate) for last 24h / 7d
Dashboard: per-route aggregated throughput and cost estimate for selected time range
Tracing: single-request timeline with stage markers (received, queued, batch_start, model_infer_start, model_infer_end, response_sent)
Cost: aggregated cost by model and by route with time range selector and export CSV
Operations: rollout canary, feature flag gated behind console-2025.04 flag, basic metrics instrumented for SLO monitoring
scope_removed: Custom dashboards and drag-drop widget editor
Per-token cost breakdown and token-level audit views
Span flamegraphs, per-layer kernel timings, and stack traces in tracing UI
Alerting rules and synthetic transaction monitors
Long-term retention > 30 days for detailed traces and raw telemetry
Federated dashboards (combining console telemetry with external billing systems)
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard model summary page loads within 1.5s (95th) for orgs with <= 5M requests/day
Model summary shows P50 and P95 latency and error rate for selected range; numbers reconcile with internal metrics pipeline within 1% error
Per-route throughput and cost estimate matches billing API totals to within 2% for daily aggregates (sanity checked against billing-report PR #245)
Tracing UI surfaces request timeline with the expected stage markers; sample trace for a known request ID displays full timeline and latency buckets
Exported CSV for cost page contains columns: date, model, route, total_requests, total_cost_usd; file validated against server-side aggregation job
Feature flag present and used by rollout plan; canary group (5% of orgs) sees new UI, remainder see legacy or hidden surface
E2E smoke tests for the dashboard/tracing/cost pages pass in CI and in a staging cluster with synthetic traffic
notes: Engineering estimate revised down after removing custom widgets and retention (>30d) dependencies
PM/Eng/Design sync 2025-02-14: agreed to prioritize accuracy of aggregates and reconciliation with billing over feature richness
Design provided simplified mockups (link) focusing on summary cards and compact trace timeline — see links
Follow-up tickets created for post-launch features and dependencies: PM-11235 (custom-dashboard backlog), PM-11236 (token-cost-analysis), PM-11237 (trace-retention-radar)
Flagging potential UX risk: power users may request token-level debug; add support doc describing path to request extended visibility via dedicated support
